priorStories.headline: Attack at Jordan church funeral kills seven
priorStories.body:
Gunmen attacked mourners during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Humud village, killing seven people and injuring 40, Jordanian authorities said.

The government described the shooting as a terrorist attack and said security forces were pursuing those responsible. Jordan declared three days of national mourning beginning October 23.

priorStories.headline: U.S. cuts staffing at four Mideast embassies
priorStories.body:
The United States reduced staffing at its embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The embassies remained open.

A memo sent October 23 by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said intelligence indicated that Iran had substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel and that alleged plotting had reached advanced stages. U.S. officials also connected threats from Iran and Yemen’s Houthi movement to the staffing changes.

candidates.summary: A critically injured victim of the October 23 attack on mourners at a Greek Orthodox church in Hmoud village died Saturday morning, raising the death toll from seven to eight, according to the director of Prince Ali Military Hospital. Another patient remained in critical condition.
candidates.title: Jordan church attack death toll rises to eight

candidates.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen’s Houthi movement toward Riyadh. It also reported intercepting a drone over the Eastern Province. Civil Defense alerts were issued in several locations and later lifted; no casualties or damage were immediately reported.
candidates.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missile headed toward Riyadh

candidates.summary: Israeli forces imposed widespread closures in Hebron and continued a multi-day operation begun after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers on October 23. The military restricted movement through designated exits, while Palestinian accounts reported residents displaced from some homes and roads blocked across the city.
candidates.title: Israeli forces impose widespread closures in Hebron

candidates.summary: Taiwan’s Central Emergency Operations Center reported Saturday that Typhoon Champi had left one person dead and 527 injured. Most injuries were attributed to falling trees, power cables, billboards and damaged water pipes. The Central Weather Administration later downgraded Champi to a tropical storm and lifted its land warning.
candidates.title: Taiwan reports 527 injuries from Typhoon Champi
